messages:
beth-customer: Hey team — our nightly deploys to prod started failing around 03:10 UTC with 401s to Redwood API. This started right after we rotated our internal CI signing keys. Error from pipeline log: `token verification failed: invalid signature`. Can we escalate?

jess-support: Sorry you're hitting this, @beth-customer. Can you paste the minimal curl your CI is using to call Redwood and a sanitized log snippet? Also which auth method are you using (API key, signed JWT, oauth)?

beth-customer: We use a short-lived JWT signed by our CI service account (internal signing key rotation), then exchange it for a Redwood API token via our proxy. Minimal curl (sanitized):

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDSIGNED_JWT" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-core-2","input":"test"}'
```

Log snippet from job (redacted):
```
2026-03-16T03:10:12Z pipeline: request=abc123 status=401 err="token verification failed: invalid signature (kid not found)"
2026-03-16T03:10:12Z pipeline: exchange failed for job=deploy-2026-03-16
```

We rotated the signing key at 03:00 UTC and updated the CI config, but maybe there's a rollout delay.

sam-eng: Thanks — that error (`kid not found`) suggests the JWT header contains a key id that Redwood's verification layer doesn't recognize. Two likely causes: 1) CI is still signing with a new kid but the key metadata hasn't propagated to the Redwood token-introspection cache, or 2) the signing key changed but the JWKS entry wasn't published under the old key id.

mike-sre: Also check if your proxy is doing any caching of the JWKS or token metadata. We saw similar when an internal KMS rotated keys and the JWKS endpoint returned a new set while caches still had old entries. What does your JWKS endpoint look like (url)? Is it behind a CDN?

beth-customer: JWKS is at https://auth.company/jwks.json — it's behind our edge CDN with 60s TTL. We did push new keys to JWKS at 03:00. CI logs show signing kid `kid: sk-new-2026-03` and the JWKS now contains that kid.

jess-support: Can you confirm the exact error body from Redwood API (full response)? If you have a request id we can trace on our side.

beth-customer: Full response:
```
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "error": "invalid_token",
  "error_description": "signature verification failed: unknown kid=\"sk-new-2026-03\"",
  "request_id": "rwd-0b6f3e4c"
}
```
Request id included above.

sam-eng: Got the request id, thanks — we'll pull the logs. Quick interim suggestions:
- Rollback CI signing to the previous key if you can (fastest way to restore).
- If rollback not possible, confirm your JWKS cache TTL at every hop (CDN, proxy, our edge).
- As a workaround, create a short-lived API key in Redwood Console for the pipeline to use while we trace. Make it scoped to deploy-only permissions (least privilege).

mike-sre: I'm seeing a trace for rwd-0b6f3e4c — request arrived at 03:10:12 UTC, token header `kid=sk-new-2026-03` — our verifier fetched JWKS from https://auth.company/jwks.json at 03:08:59 but the response body didn't include `sk-new-2026-03` (it returned old keys). Later fetch at 03:09:34 returned the new set. There's a 25s window where our verifier saw the old list and concluded kid unknown. Our code caches JWKS for 60s by default which caused the failure.

jess-support: Thanks @mike-sre, that matches a transient race between key publish and our JWKS cache TTL. We're going to patch the verifier to attempt one background refresh on unknown kid (for a short grace) and to log these events more verbosely. For your org: reduce TTL on your CDN or configure a pre-warm publish at key rotation start so keys are available before CI resumes.

beth-customer: We can reduce TTL but the rotation is managed by a separate team — asking them to coordinate pre-warm. For now we spun up a scoped Redwood API key (deploy-bot-ci) and updated the pipeline; deploys are green again.

sam-eng: Good temporary mitigation. We're filing an internal bug to improve resiliency — patch target: 1 week, low-risk hotfix to try one immediate JWKS refresh on unknown kid and a clearer admin message referencing request_id. I've attached the internal bug: INF-4021.

infra-bot: Incident created: INF-4021 — "JWKS race causing transient token reject on key rotation". Priority: P2. Assignee: sam-eng. Link: https://redwood.internal/issue/INF-4021

jess-support: Leaving this thread open until you've confirmed the rotation process is updated. Also recommended next steps for you (short list):
- Create a dedicated CI service account in your identity provider with a deterministic key-rotation window and pre-publish keys before CI rebind.
- Use least-privilege Redwood API key where possible for automated jobs (token exchange fallback).
- Add a pre-rotation smoke check that fetches `/jwks.json` and verifies the new kid is present.

beth-customer: Great advice, thanks. I'll coordinate with keys team to add a pre-publish hook and we'll keep the temporary API key until rotation workflow is updated. Leaving notes in our runbook.

jess-support: Glad it's recovered. Marking this as customer escalated -> resolved with mitigation. If you want the hotfix backported for JWKS retry, I can request that from infra.

beth-customer: Please do request the hotfix so we have less blast radius next rotation. Thanks all :thumbsup:

mike-sre: Filed hotfix request for JWKS retry + improved logging. Tracking INF-4021 -> will update here when merged.
